LESSON: FOOTBALL

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS
Strand: Creating and Performing
Topic 2.8: Football

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Football. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can colours be used to show distance?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. perform dribbling skill in football
2. create a pictorial composition using crayon etching inspired by football game
3. value team effort in a football game and crayon etched drawing

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: FOOTBALL
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Football helps you succeed in CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: FOOTBALL
Study Football like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Perform dribbling skill in football

What this means
In this part you learn to perform dribbling skill in football. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: perform dribbling skill in football.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Football” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can perform dribbling skill in football. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Create a pictorial composition using crayon etching inspired by football game

What this means
In this part you learn to create a pictorial composition using crayon etching inspired by football game. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: create a pictorial composition using crayon etching inspired by football game.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Football in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can create a pictorial composition using crayon etching inspired by football game. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Value team effort in a football game and crayon etched drawing

What this means
In this part you learn to value team effort in a football game and crayon etched drawing. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: value team effort in a football game and crayon etched drawing.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can value team effort in a football game and crayon etched drawing. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Football is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Football” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: perform dribbling skill in football)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Football in your own words. (skill: create a pictorial composition using crayon etching inspired by football game)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: value team effort in a football game and crayon etched drawing)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Football to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: perform dribbling skill in football.
3. Practise this skill: create a pictorial composition using crayon etching inspired by football game.
4. Practise this skill: value team effort in a football game and crayon etched drawing.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Football from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Football: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Football?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can colours be used to show distance?
2. Why is ball control important in a football match?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Football means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: perform dribbling skill in football.
5. Be able to: create a pictorial composition using crayon etching inspired by football game.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
